reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: We pick the issue tracker that fits our workflow, plugs into our code and release tools, and won't slow us down as we grow.

scenarios.label: Enterprise standardization
scenarios.description: CTO/CIO consolidates engineering onto a single tracker under security, compliance, and procurement oversight.

scenarios.label: Migrating from legacy tracker
scenarios.description: Moving off an aging on-prem/bespoke or unsupported tool to a modern cloud tracker without losing history or workflow fidelity.

scenarios.label: Outgrowing lightweight boards
scenarios.description: A scaling team replaces simple kanban/docs with a tracker that supports custom workflows, permissions, and reporting.

scenarios.label: Founder-led startup pick
scenarios.description: A small startup chooses its first tracker during early team setup to get shipping quickly.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Enterprise standardization|generic] Leadership wants one way for 30+ engineering teams to plan and report. Right now it's spreadsheets, email threads, and homegrown tools. I can't roll up status, dependencies slip, audits are painful. What kind of system would actually centralize this without killing dev flow?

[problem_recognition|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] Stuck on a 2009-era app where we log bugs and tasks. No real API, permissions are flaky, search is slow, and the workflow can't match how we work now. We need to move tens of thousands of records and keep history and links to commits. How do teams replace something like this without losing data?

[problem_recognition|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] We started with simple cards-in-columns. Now we've got multiple squads, epics, release trains, and approvals. Cards feel too flat, reporting is copy-paste hell, and cross-team dependencies are invisible. What do people use when the sticky-notes phase runs out?

[problem_recognition|Founder-led startup pick|generic] Founder here. 18 engineers, weekly releases. Our mix of docs + chat + a basic board is dropping balls on dependencies and code reviews. I need one place that ties work to repos, has sane permissions, and doesn't eat my weekends to administer. What should I be building or buying to fix this?

[category_education|-|generic] What does project management software actually do for a software team? Plain English please - how it handles planning, sprints, bugs, roadmaps, and reporting, with real-world examples.

[discovery|Enterprise standardization|generic] Best project management platforms for standardizing process across a large engineering org (20+ teams)? Needs centralized admin, flexible workflows, cross-team reporting, audit logs/compliance, SSO, and solid APIs.

[discovery|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] Best project management tools for replacing an ancient internal bug database? Priority on migration: CSV/API import, field mapping, history retention, ID preservation, and linking to repos/CI.

[discovery|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] Best project management options for teams moving beyond simple boards? Need epics, dependencies, automation, multi-team planning, and real reporting without a ton of overhead.

[discovery|Founder-led startup pick|generic] As a founder picking our first real project management system for a dev-heavy startup: what are the best options that integrate tightly with our git repos, are API-first, quick to set up, and won't crush us on price as we grow to about 50 engineers?

[shortlist|Enterprise standardization|generic] Shortlist 3 - 5 project management platforms suited for standardizing process across 20+ engineering teams. Must have centralized admin, custom workflows, portfolio-level reporting, audit/compliance features, SSO, and robust APIs.

[shortlist|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] Give me 3 - 4 project management tools that are strong at migrating from a legacy system: good importers, scriptable field mapping, history retention, ID preservation, and repo/CI integrations.

[shortlist|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] Can you shortlist three project management options that are a real step up from simple boards for software teams - epics, dependencies, iterations, backlogs, automation, and solid reports?

[shortlist|Founder-led startup pick|generic] I'm the founder. Shortlist three project management platforms that are API-friendly, integrate cleanly with git, lightweight to administer, and can scale from 10 to 100 engineers without crazy pricing. Brief why each.

[criteria|Enterprise standardization|generic] We're picking one project management tool as the enterprise standard. What really matters to compare? thinking scale, security/compliance, admin controls, integrations, reporting, total cost to run.
[criteria|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] Migrating off a 10-year-old on-prem bug tracker. What criteria should drive the shortlist so the move is painless now and maintainable later?
[criteria|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] we've outgrown simple kanban boards. for a dev org, what should we prioritize when moving to something more powerful?

[criteria|Founder-led startup pick|generic] founder here choosing our first serious tracker for a 10-engineer startup. give me a spec-style checklist of must haves vs nice to haves so i can make a clean call.

[feature_screening|Enterprise standardization|generic] Which platforms support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, org-wide roles with fine-grained project permissions, data residency controls, and exportable audit logs?

[feature_screening|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] Which tools can import from a legacy tracker via CSV or API, map custom fields, bring over attachments and comments, preserve original IDs, and keep issue links intact?

[feature_screening|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] looking for options that have epics > stories > subtasks, dependency tracking, sprint planning with burndown, and automation rules out of the box. which ones do?

[feature_screening|Founder-led startup pick|generic] For a small engineering team, which trackers let me define custom state machines, expose a solid REST/GraphQL API with webhooks, and include built-in roadmap/timeline views?

[use_case|Enterprise standardization|generic] We are consolidating 50+ teams into one system: need portfolio rollups, program boards, shared backlogs, cross-team dependency views, approvals, and exec dashboards. How would you model and configure that?

[use_case|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] about 200k issues in an old on-prem tracker, lots of custom fields, attachments, and cross-links. want to migrate with near-zero downtime and keep history searchable. outline the steps and gotchas.

[use_case|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] two scrum teams. simple boards aren't cutting it. need backlog refinement with estimates, sprint capacity planning, velocity, and tighter permissions. how do we move up without burying folks in process?

[use_case|Founder-led startup pick|generic] 12-person startup shipping weekly. want a lean setup: intake from support/sales, triage to eng, lightweight roadmap, sprint planning, and auto-linking commits and PRs from our source control. how would you wire that in one tool plus minimal integrations?

[social_validation|-|generic] What do software teams actually use and rate well right now for project tracking? point me to credible review sources or community threads, and any adoption data by team size if available.

[comparison|Enterprise standardization|Asana] We're consolidating tooling for about 1,200 engineers across 60 squads. Jira vs Asana at enterprise scale: performance on huge backlogs, granular permissions, audit logs, SSO/SCIM, sandboxes, advanced roadmapping, cross-project reporting. Any migration or admin gotchas we should expect?

[comparison|Migrating from legacy tracker|Monday.com] Moving off an old on-prem tracker with 10 years of history and tons of custom fields. For the migration, how does Jira compare to Monday.com on import fidelity (comments, attachments, workflows), issue hierarchy, automations, two-way sync during cutover, and API rate limits?

[comparison|Outgrowing lightweight boards|Trello] We've basically outgrown Trello. For a dev team running sprints, is switching to Jira worth it? How different are backlog grooming, estimates, dependencies, and permissions, and can non-engineers still have simple kanban boards without getting lost?

[comparison|Founder-led startup pick|ClickUp] Founder here choosing between Jira and ClickUp for 12 engineers. Need: epic/story/subtask hierarchy, sprint rituals, GitHub PR linking, automations, solid API, docs/wikis, fine-grained permissions, SOC2, EU data residency, mobile offline. Which fits better for a lean team and why?

[objections|Enterprise standardization|generic] Real question: does Jira bog down at enterprise scale? Thinking thousands of issues per project, lots of boards and filters, heavy JQL and dashboards. What page load times do people actually see, and what config or arch choices keep it fast?

[objections|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] If we move to Jira from our creaky on-prem tracker, are we swapping clunky for slow? We'd be importing about 500k issues with full history. Do boards, searches, and backlogs stay responsive after a big migration, or does it crawl?

[objections|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] Thinking of jumping to Jira because our simple boards hit the ceiling. Honest take on speed: will day-to-day stuff feel sluggish? Board load times with swimlanes and quick filters, backlog scrolling with thousands of tickets, search latency?

[objections|Founder-led startup pick|generic] I'm worried Jira might slow a small team down. For 10 - 15 engineers, how snappy is it in practice? Typical page loads, keyboard nav, board interactions, mobile app speed. Is Jira Cloud fast enough without stripping plugins to the bone?

[pricing|Enterprise standardization|generic] For standardizing across the org, what really drives total cost in this category? Per-seat vs feature add-ons, SSO/SCIM, data residency, admin features, support SLAs. Any hidden costs like sandbox environments, audit exports, or training we should budget for?

[pricing|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] If we go with Jira for about 300 users, which tier usually fits a regulated org: Standard, Premium, or Enterprise? We need IP allowlisting, stronger admin controls, and Advanced Roadmaps. Ballpark pricing, annual vs monthly, and any migration credits or discounts?

[pricing|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] We're moving off a free board tool. Is paying for a full project management platform actually worth it for a 30-person dev team? What features tend to justify the spend, and any gotchas going from free to paid (seat minimums, add-ons)?

[pricing|Founder-led startup pick|generic] Help me run the math for a seed-stage team: Jira Standard vs Premium for 12 seats, monthly vs annual, expected first-year total. Include likely add-ons for time tracking and roadmaps. Is there a free tier we can start on without locking ourselves into a bad upgrade path?

[business_case|Enterprise standardization|generic] Need to get our CFO on board with standardizing on Jira across engineering. What's the simplest way to show total cost vs upside (governance, compliance, fewer tools to support, delivery metrics) in dollars and risk terms?

[business_case|Migrating from legacy tracker|generic] Pitch help: migrating from our aging on-prem tracker to Jira. CFO is worried about migration cost, downtime, and change management. How do I quantify the payback and de-risk the move?

[business_case|Outgrowing lightweight boards|generic] We've outgrown simple kanban boards and spreadsheets. I want to make the case to finance for moving to Jira for real workflows, permissions, and reporting. How would you frame ROI and the ramp cost so it lands with a CFO?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] Be honest: we've been on Jira for years and it feels heavy lately. Licenses are up, some teams complain about speed and admin sprawl. How do I tell if we should tune it vs start evaluating other options?
[alternatives|-|defensive] If we didn't use Jira, what would you recommend instead for a dev org running Scrum and Kanban with code reviews and CI ties? Looking for serious options, not toy boards.
[alternatives|-|Asana] What are better Asana alternatives for software engineering teams that need backlogs, sprints, release tracking, and tight repo/CI integration?
[alternatives|-|Monday.com] Alternatives to Monday.com for a product + engineering org? Need real issue tracking, branching/PR linking, and customizable workflows, not just task lists.
[alternatives|-|Trello] Trello is hitting its limits for our dev teams. What tools should we look at that handle epics, sprints, and complex workflows?
[alternatives|-|ClickUp] ClickUp feels cluttered for our engineers. What are stronger options built for software teams with backlog grooming, sprint boards, and good API/extensibility?
[renewal|-|generic] Renewal time for Jira. Worth keeping at about 600 seats, or are there meaningfully cheaper tools that won't blow up our dev workflows and reporting?

[problem_resolution|-|generic] Jira Cloud: transitions disappeared on a bunch of issues after we switched a project to company-managed. Users can't move tickets out of In Progress. Where do I check first - workflow conditions, permission schemes, or something else - to fix this without breaking active sprints?

[expansion|-|generic] We're happy with Jira for dev and product. Thinking about rolling it out to more teams and using it for release planning and incident follow-ups. What setup changes or add-ons make that scale work without turning it into a mess?

[ecosystem|-|generic] For teams building software, what integrations and plugins pair best with Jira for source control, CI/CD, docs, chat, and test management? Looking for the ones engineers actually adopt.

[advocacy|-|generic] we run our sprints and bug triage in Jira. new VP says it's too complex and wants us on something "simpler." how do i make a solid, dev-focused case to keep Jira? looking for concrete points: custom workflows, issue types, JQL, git/PR links, automations, release tracking, permissions/audit trail, reporting for retros. also any setup tips so PMs don't feel it's heavy but engineers still get the power we need.
